project_interpretations: Regular chain pointers are at most MAXREGSECT; the final pointer is ENDOFCHAIN.
No sector belongs to more than one chain and no chain contains a cycle.
The actual sector count matches the size specified for a chain.
Unallocated sectors are represented by FREESECT in the FAT.
selected_sections.title: Compound File Sector Numbers and Types

project_interpretations: The signature is D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1 and the header CLSID is zero.
Minor Version SHOULD be 0x003E for Major Version 3 or 4.
Major Version is 3 or 4, with sector shifts 9 or 12 respectively.
Byte Order is 0xFFFE, Mini Sector Shift is 6, and the six reserved bytes are zero.
Mini Stream Cutoff Size is 0x00001000.
The version 4 header-sector padding after byte 512 is zero.
selected_sections.title: Compound File Header

project_interpretations: Every physical sector is represented by the FAT, including free sectors.
FAT entries beyond physical end-of-file are FREESECT.
Mini-sector offsets are mini-sector number multiplied by 64 within the mini stream.
The mini stream is a normal FAT chain rooted by directory stream ID 0.
The final DIFAT link is ENDOFCHAIN and FAT/DIFAT allocation markers match their sector roles.
selected_sections.title: FAT, Mini FAT, and DIFAT Sectors

project_interpretations: Directory stream ID 0 is the root storage entry and its name is Root Entry.
The root directory entry color is irrelevant because that entry has no siblings.
Each sibling-tree root is black and two consecutive sibling nodes are not both red.
Sibling names are unique and sorted by UTF-16 name length, then simple uppercase code units.
The MS-CFB sibling-tree rules do not impose the classical equal-black-height invariant.
Streams below the 4096-byte cutoff use mini FAT; larger streams use FAT.
Unused directory entries are zero except for three NOSTREAM sibling/child pointers.
selected_sections.title: Directory Entries and Sibling Trees

project_interpretations: Application stream bytes are arbitrary and are not semantically validated by MS-CFB.
Each user-data chain has one directory entry and enough allocated bytes for its declared size.
The unused tail of a user-data sector SHOULD be zero, but a preservation inventory must retain observed nonzero tails.
When required above 2 GiB, the range-lock sector is FAT-allocated as ENDOFCHAIN and is not used by structural chains.

record.text: A stream that specifies designer module properties. MUST contain data as specified by VBFrame Stream (section 2.3.5). Name of this stream MUST start with the UTF-16 character 0x0003 followed by the UTF-16 string "VBFrame" (case-insensitive).
The VBFrame stream specifies the extended property values of a designer.

This stream is an array of bytes that specifies the extended property values of a designer module. MUST contain MBCS characters encoded using the code page specified in PROJECTCODEPAGE (section 2.3.4.2.1.5).

Property values of the designer are set at design-time. Property values are used at run-time as specified to initialize the designer. For example, a designer can be used at run time to display data to and accept data from a user and the following properties could be used to determine the location of the designer.
VBFrameText = "VERSION 5.00" NWLN "Begin" 1*WSP DesignerCLSID 1*WSP DesignerName *WSP NWLN DesignerProperties "End" NWLN

<DesignerCLSID>: Specifies the class identifier (CLSID) of the designer. The Automation type library that contains the designer specified MUST be referenced with a REFERENCECONTROL (section 2.3.4.2.2.3). The value "{C62A69F0-16DC-11CE-9E98-00AA00574A4F}" specifies the designer is an Office Form ActiveX control specified in [MS-OFORMS].
<DesignerName>: Specifies the name of the designer module associated with the properties.
Specifies the VBA-specific extended properties of a designer.
Specifies the title text of the designer.
Specifies the height of the designer in twips.
Specifies the left edge of the designer in twips relative to the window specified by DesignerStartupPosition (section 2.3.5.11).
Specifies the position of the top edge of the designer in twips relative to the window specified by DesignerStartupPosition (section 2.3.5.11).
Specifies the width of the designer in twips.
Specifies whether the designer is enabled. The default is TRUE.
Specifies the Help topic identifier associated with this designer in the Help file as specified by ProjectHelpFile (section 2.3.1.9).
Specifies that the designer be shown with right and left coordinates reversed for right-to-left language use.
Specifies whether the designer is a modal window. The default is TRUE.
Specifies the startup position of the designer as follows.
<RelativeParent>: Specifies the window used to determine the relative starting coordinates of the control window.
MUST be one of the following values:
"Manual" mode. DesignerTop (section 2.3.5.5) and DesignerLeft (section 2.3.5.4) coordinates of the designer are relative to the desktop window.
"CenterOwner" mode. Center the designer relative to its parent window.
"Center" mode. Center the designer relative to the desktop window.
"WindowsDefault" mode. Place the designer in the upper-left corner of screen.
Specifies user-defined data associated with the designer.
Specifies the number of times the designer has been changed and saved. The default is 0.
Specifies whether the designer is visible. The default is TRUE.
Specifies whether a help button is shown for the designer. The default is FALSE.
Specifies whether a help topic is associated with this designer. The Help topic identifier is specified by DesignerHelpContextId (section 2.3.5.8).

 ClientLeft = 45

End

record.text: The module header is a set of attributes consisting of name/value pairs that specify the certain linguistic characteristics of a module. While a module header could be directly written by a human programmer, more typically a VBA implementation will mechanically generate module headers based upon the programmer’s usage of implementation specific tools. These tools are not part of the scope of this document, so their contents, including the version and all text between "BEGIN" and "END" at the start of the file is not part of the module body and is not required to conform to the VBA grammar.
